parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, state registration, or documented border screening is recorded, so no tier-1 state exposure appears. But the outed visitor faces documented routine denial of medical care (including general treatment such as malaria therapy), zero anti-discrimination protection, religious framing of transgender people as demons, and commonplace civilian lynching violence that police rarely investigate — victims conceal identity fearing mistreatment. Recourse is thin: two of fifteen 2023 UPR recommendations accepted, LGBTI organisations unregistrable, legal gender recognition impossible. Violence magnitude is unresolved (single 2024 source, no count or denominator), so it is weighted as patterned but unquantified, not a campaign. Combined: hostile society plus passive state with effectively no remedy, but no imprisonment or execution pathway for trans status.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No source addresses airport screening, document markers, or entry procedures for trans travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Any document-mismatch exposure would feed into an encounter with police, whose responsiveness to LGBTQ victims is documented as poor.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police rarely pursue perpetrators of anti-LGBTQ violence; those reporting conceal orientation or gender identity out of fear of mistreatment. No documented arrest of trans people for status itself.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented custody protocol for trans detainees either way; accepted 2023 UPR pledge to investigate anti-LGBTQ violence is unshown in operation.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A trans visitor reporting an assault enters the same police channel documented as avoided by locals.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: One foreign-government report records hostility especially outside major urban areas — a single reporting year, not a standing map; no named regions.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented for rural or urban areas.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Itinerary outside major cities plausibly raises exposure to documented hostility, but the record does not license specific locational risk.

care_services.exposure: LGBTQI+ persons routinely refused medical care including hormone therapy and general treatment such as malaria; no legal protection against refusal. An outed traveller needing emergency care is directly exposed.
care_services.protection: None documented for visitors; sex-harassment and data-protection provisions do not reach care denial.
care_services.interaction: Medical need forces disclosure; refusal then interacts with police non-responsiveness and no remedy.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Priests documented calling transgender people demons; conversion therapy by imams, priests and traditional healers; homosexuality widely viewed as unnatural disease. Law bars none of this explicitly on gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Article 552 penalises electronic incitement to hatred on sexual-orientation grounds (one year, 5m CFA); coverage of gender identity unstated and no enforcement record.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Religious framing supplies social license for service refusal and violence that police then do not pursue.

minors_guardians.exposure: Conversion therapy commonly coerced by families; a child in the travelling party could face hostility, but no visitor-specific rule is documented. Children's Code adoption bar is resident-facing.
minors_guardians.protection: Youth shelters exist (20-place centre since ~2020, ~380 young people) but are resident/sub-regional, not traveller-accessible by record.
minors_guardians.interaction: No documented interaction between a trans parent's status and entry, custody, or services.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Anti-gay lynchings described as commonplace in an April 2024 report, mostly by civilians, police rarely pursuing perpetrators. No count, period, denominator, or homicide-rate comparison, so magnitude unresolved.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Accepted 2023 UPR recommendation to investigate and prosecute violence; no operational record. Small shelter infrastructure exists.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A trans visitor assaulted has no documented effective channel; fear of police mistreatment discourages reporting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No discrimination law covering gender identity, legal gender recognition impossible, LGBTI organisations cannot register, government rejected most UPR recommendations.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Digital Code data-protection provisions, incitement penalty, two accepted UPR recommendations, small survivor-support shelters.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper data protections do not offset service denial or unpunished street violence experienced by an outed visitor.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra imposes a state border register excluding trans visitors — a tier-1 universal exposure absent here, where no border rule is documented. This dossier instead rates on tier-3 societal hostility plus care denial with no recourse. Similar tier, different mechanism: worse care/violence severity, but no state exclusion machinery or failing-appeal apparatus.

Kestrel Isles shows administrative secondary screening with written reasons, appeal desk and consular notification, ending in refused admission rather than prosecution. This jurisdiction is materially lower: routine medical-care denial, commonplace unpunished lynching violence, and police avoidance outweigh that anchor's humiliation-plus-delay severity.

Meridia features transport police as active perpetrators — extortion, document confiscation, overnight cells. Here police are passive rather than predatory: no state-perpetrated targeting, no extortion, no trans-status arrest documented. That keeps this rating above 0.25 despite comparable-or-worse societal violence and equally thin remedies.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a hostile society with a passive, non-protective state. Absence of trans-specific criminalisation and undocumented border practice rule out tier-1 and much of tier-2 exposure. What governs is documented routine refusal of medical care reaching any outed traveller who falls ill, religious demonisation of transgender people, and patterned civilian violence that police decline to pursue — with victims conceal identity because police are feared. Recourse machinery (UPR pledges, data protections, incitement law) is paper without shown operation, and LGBTI groups cannot even register. Violence magnitude is genuinely unresolved, so it is counted as patterned but unquantified rather than as a campaign. Result: elevated-to-high risk band — deterred daily life and real assault/care-denial severity, but no imprisonment or execution pathway for trans status itself.
